While mechanistically similar to OntoCoDec's token-level filtering, PICARD operates over a \emph{fixed, fully enumerated} schema---database table and column names known before decoding begins.
In contrast, OntoCoDec's entity registry is populated \emph{during} generation as entity spans are extracted from free text, requiring constraint sets that evolve with the decoding prefix---a fundamental distinction between querying a known schema and extracting from unstructured text.
Synchromesh~\cite{synchromesh_iclr2022} pioneers Constrained Semantic Decoding (CSD), which enforces syntax, type, and scope constraints simultaneously during code generation from pre-trained LMs without fine-tuning, establishing that semantic constraints can be expressed as dynamic token masks conditioned on the generation prefix.
MGD~\cite{mgd_neurips2023} uses static-analysis monitors to perform incremental type checking at decode time, enabling SantaCoder-1.1B to outperform text-davinci-003 on repository-level code completion by ensuring that every generated identifier is type-correct with respect to the surrounding code context.
Most recently, \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile full type systems---including generic types and subtyping---into prefix automata for token-level logits masking, reducing compilation errors by over 50\%.
This last system is the closest mechanistic analog to OntoCoDec, applying the same ``type system $\to$ automaton $\to$ logits mask'' pipeline, though in a fundamentally different domain.
The key technical difference lies in the constraint structure: programming-language type systems feature deep subtyping hierarchies and parametric polymorphism, whereas IE ontology axioms specify flat domain/range sets---a relation $R$ accepts head entities from set $\mathcal{D}(R)$ and tail entities from set $\mathcal{R}(R)$, with no subtype chains.
Conversely, IE introduces a challenge absent in code generation: the constraint target (entity type) must be inferred from free-text spans rather than read from declared type annotations, requiring a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation.
These methods collectively demonstrate that semantic (type) constraints at decode time are both feasible and highly effective, but exclusively in the code domain where type systems are formally specified.
OntoCoDec is the first to \emph{automatically compile} IE ontology axioms---including domain/range constraints---into token-level decoding masks for information extraction, migrating the type-constrained decoding paradigm from code generation to IE.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 2: Vocabulary/Type-Constrained Generation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Vocabulary and Type-Constrained Generation.}
The idea of enforcing entity-type compatibility constraints for information extraction dates back to pre-neural methods.
\citet{roth_yih_2004} formulate joint entity and relation identification as an integer linear program (ILP) that enforces type constraints---e.g., \textsc{Emp-Org} only between \textsc{Per} and \textsc{Org} entities---establishing the foundational principle that relational type compatibility should be a hard constraint, not a soft preference learned from data.
In the autoregressive era, GENRE~\cite{decao2021genre} pioneers trie-based constrained beam search for autoregressive entity retrieval, restricting each decoding step to tokens consistent with valid entity names from a predefined catalog.
GenIE~\cite{josifoski2022genie} extends this approach to end-to-end information extraction with state-based constraints that enforce valid triple structures, achieving strong performance on closed-world knowledge base population, though it requires task-specific fine-tuning on the target schema.
AdaKGC~\cite{adakgc_emnlp2023} introduces schema-constrained dynamic decoding with trie-based prefix trees that adapt to the target schema, enforcing that generated entity and relation names belong to a predefined inventory---a vocabulary-level constraint that ensures name validity but does not verify type compatibility between a relation and its arguments.
GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} provides a unified grammar-constrained decoding framework for structured NLP tasks including IE, introducing input-dependent grammars that adapt constraints based on the source text---the closest precursor to OntoCoDec in applying logits masking to IE, though limited to syntactic constraints.
NeuroLogic Decoding~\cite{lu2021neurologic} expresses lexical inclusion and exclusion constraints as predicate logic formulas enforced during beam search, offering a general mechanism for token-level control that can encode vocabulary membership but not relational type rules.
These approaches constrain \emph{which tokens} can appear (vocabulary membership) but not \emph{which type combinations} are valid for a given relation.
OntoCoDec's semantic layer enforces relational constraints---e.g., that the head entity of relation $R$ must belong to type set $\mathcal{D}(R)$---which cannot be expressed as static vocabulary restrictions because the valid set depends on the relation type generated earlier in the same sequence.
While Roth \& Yih's ILP formulation shares the same type-compatibility motivation, it operates as a post-hoc reranker over discrete candidates; OntoCoDec integrates enforcement directly into autoregressive decoding, preventing violations rather than filtering them.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 3: Structural Constraints for IE
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training and Prompting.}
An orthogonal approach encodes IE output structure through model training or prompt design rather than decoding-time enforcement, relying on learned representations to produce schema-compliant outputs.
UIE~\cite{lu2022uie} defines a Structured Extraction Language and trains a unified text-to-structure model across 13 IE datasets, relying on large-scale pre-training to internalize output format constraints.
GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} expresses annotation guidelines as Python dataclass definitions and fine-tunes Code-LLaMA to generate typed code, achieving strong zero-shot transfer to unseen IE schemas by leveraging the implicit type structure of programming languages.
KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024} takes this further by encoding 29K entity types from Wikidata as a Python class hierarchy, training a Code-LLM to generate structured extraction code that implicitly respects type inheritance---the most comprehensive schema-as-code approach to date.
CodeIE~\cite{li2023codeie} similarly reformulates IE as code generation, leveraging the structural regularity of programming languages to reduce output format errors.
ADELIE~\cite{qi2024adelie} uses SFT and DPO to align LLMs on IE tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results among open-source models while preserving general capabilities, though compliance with ontological constraints remains a learned soft preference rather than a guarantee.
In the supervised setting, joint entity-relation architectures such as SpERT~\cite{eberts2020spert} and PFN~\cite{yan2021pfn} enforce type consistency implicitly through shared representations: SpERT classifies entity spans and relation pairs in a single BERT pass with span-level negative sampling, while PFN decomposes feature encoding into entity-specific, relation-specific, and shared partitions via gating mechanisms.
These models achieve strong performance but are limited to fixed, predefined schemas and cannot generalize to unseen ontologies without retraining---precisely the zero-shot, ontology-portable scenario that OntoCoDec targets.
EnriCo~\cite{zaratiana2024enrico} applies Answer Set Programming (ASP) constraints during decoding of joint entity-relation extraction models, enforcing structural type compatibility at generation time---a decoding-time approach, though with model-specific, manually authored constraints rather than ontology-driven compilation.
Training-based methods provide \emph{soft} structural guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but cannot guarantee compliance at inference time, as demonstrated by non-trivial violation rates even in fine-tuned systems.
Importantly, training-based and decoding-time approaches are complementary rather than competing: a system like GoLLIE could be combined with OntoCoDec's constraint layers, using fine-tuning to maximize the probability of valid outputs while decoding-time enforcement eliminates residual violations.
OntoCoDec provides \emph{hard} decoding-time enforcement that is training-free, automatically compiled from ontology schemas, and composable with any of these training-based approaches.

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 4: Type-Checking / Ontology Validation
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
Rather than constraining generation, several methods validate LLM outputs against ontological rules after generation, applying a detect-then-fix paradigm.
ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} dynamically generates ontology snippets containing domain/range constraints as prompt context, achieving 98.8\% precision across 195 predicates at web scale---but constraint adherence relies on prompt-level guidance, not enforcement, leaving residual violations unaddressed.
SPIRES/OntoGPT~\cite{spires_2024} provides an ontology-based extraction framework that grounds LLM outputs against OBO ontologies post-generation, validating extracted entities and relations through ontology lookup and correcting mismatches in a second pass---representing the prompt-then-validate paradigm in the biomedical domain.
OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation to LLM-generated knowledge graphs, iteratively re-prompting the LLM to correct constraint violations and reducing them by approximately 10$\times$ across multiple correction rounds---demonstrating the detect-then-fix paradigm's effectiveness but also its inherent multi-pass cost.
\citet{upadhyay2023openie} inject entity-type knowledge as constraints into Open IE via both constrained inference and constraint-aware training, improving F1 by 29\% on CaRB, though their constrained inference operates over a discrete candidate set rather than during autoregressive generation.
\citet{regino2025kgcurator} propose a multi-stage LLM pipeline for validating RDF triple insertions against RDFS domain/range constraints, where each validation step requires a separate LLM call---effective but computationally expensive at scale.
RELATE~\cite{olasunkanmi2025relate} addresses the alignment gap between LLM-extracted biomedical relations and standardized ontology predicates through a three-stage pipeline: ontology preprocessing with predicate embeddings, similarity-based retrieval via SapBERT, and LLM-based reranking with negation handling, achieving 94\% accuracy@10 on ChemProt.
While RELATE demonstrates effective ontology grounding for relation extraction, its constraints are applied \emph{post-extraction} through retrieval and reranking rather than during generation, and it requires domain-specific embedding models trained on biomedical corpora.
OntoCoDec enforces ontology constraints \emph{during} autoregressive decoding and requires no additional trained components beyond the base LLM.
Concurrently, \citet{zhou2026ontologytools} compile OWL ontologies into executable tool interfaces within The World Avatar framework, requiring LLM agents to invoke ontology-aware tools that enforce semantic constraints during knowledge graph construction from scientific text.
This ``ontology-to-tools'' approach shares OntoCoDec's philosophy of compiling formal ontological knowledge into runtime enforcement mechanisms, but operates at the tool-call level (constraining which API functions the agent invokes) rather than at the token level (constraining which tokens the decoder produces), and requires an agentic multi-step workflow rather than single-pass autoregressive generation.
\citet{ekaw2024_ontology_beam} introduce ontology-constrained beam scoring for clinical summarization, applying soft biases (not hard masks) during beam search to steer outputs toward ontology-compliant terms---a middle ground between unconstrained generation and hard enforcement that reduces but cannot eliminate violations.
Post-hoc validation detects violations after generation, requiring rejection or correction cycles that waste compute---in our setting, 15.37\% of generated triples contain domain/range violations under unconstrained decoding, representing substantial wasted generation effort.
OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives rather than discarding invalid outputs, with only marginal overhead from logits masking compared to the cost of regenerating or correcting violated triples.
Soft-constraint approaches such as ontology-weighted beam scoring reduce violation frequency but cannot eliminate it, whereas OntoCoDec substantially reduces violations (DR$\downarrow$94\% on SciERC, $\downarrow$45--90\% on DocRED depending on model).

% ===========================================================================
% Paradigm 5: Constrained Decoding Quality Concerns
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
A growing body of work raises concerns that constrained decoding degrades LLM generation quality, particularly for reasoning-intensive tasks where format enforcement interferes with chain-of-thought processes.
\citet{tam2024letmespeak} conduct a comprehensive evaluation showing that rigid format constraints (JSON, XML) harm performance on math and multi-hop QA benchmarks but \emph{benefit} classification-style tasks such as slot filling---a distinction directly relevant to IE, which is fundamentally an extraction (classification-like) task rather than a reasoning task.
CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane} provides theoretical analysis of why restricting outputs to narrow grammars suppresses chain-of-thought reasoning by eliminating intermediate reasoning tokens, and proposes an alternating strategy between unconstrained reasoning phases and constrained output phases to mitigate this effect.
\citet{schall2025hiddencost} conduct a systematic study across 11 models and multiple benchmarks, finding 10--30\% semantic correctness degradation on reasoning tasks under structural constraints, with larger models showing greater absolute degradation.
\citet{zhou2026snowballing} identify ``structure snowballing''---a failure mode where format compliance cognitive load traps models in repetitive structural patterns rather than improving reasoning during self-correction iterations.
These findings establish a legitimate concern for constrained decoding in reasoning-heavy applications.
However, information extraction occupies a fundamentally different regime: the model extracts entities and relations from input text rather than generating novel reasoning chains, and \citet{tam2024letmespeak}'s own results show that extraction-style tasks are robust to---or even benefit from---format constraints.
OntoCoDec addresses this concern empirically: domain/range violations decrease by 94\% on SciERC (15.37\%$\to$0.93\%) and 45--90\% on DocRED across two models, with F1-neutral impact on SciERC ($+$0.13pp, $p{=}0.58$) and significant R-F1 gains on DocRED ($p \leq 0.013$).
Critically, OntoCoDec's constraints target only type tokens (entity types, relation labels), leaving free-text spans---entity surface forms and their boundaries---entirely unconstrained, which minimizes the distribution distortion that causes quality degradation in reasoning tasks.
A two-pass variant (S2), explored in ablation (Section~5), separates extraction and constraint enforcement into distinct passes, analogous to CRANE's alternating strategy; however, our primary single-pass approach already avoids reasoning interference by constraining only type tokens while leaving free-text spans unconstrained.

% ===========================================================================
% Our Approach
% ===========================================================================
\paragraph{Our Approach.}
OntoCoDec occupies a unique position in this landscape: it is the first system to \emph{automatically compile} IE ontology schemas---including domain/range axioms---into token-level semantic masks, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement without manually authored rules.
Unlike vocabulary-constrained methods that restrict individual tokens to a fixed set, OntoCoDec enforces \emph{cross-field relational constraints} through a stateful entity registry that tracks extracted types during autoregressive generation, enabling dynamic constraint evaluation that depends on previously decoded content.
This approach is orthogonal to supervised IE methods and applicable to any autoregressive LM without model modification or additional training.
Unlike training-based IE systems, OntoCoDec is training-free and substantially reduces type violations at inference time (DR$\downarrow$94\% on SciERC, $\downarrow$45--90\% on DocRED); unlike post-hoc validation, it prevents violations rather than detecting them, redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives with significant R-F1 gains on DocRED ($p \leq 0.013$) and F1-neutral impact on SciERC.
The two constraint layers---grammar (structural) and semantic (relational)---compose via bitwise AND with an enabling dependency: the grammar layer ensures every generated type token belongs to the valid vocabulary, which enables the semantic layer to look up and enforce domain/range rules for that type.

9	\paragraph{CF Dual Mechanism.}
10	CF violations arise from two distinct mechanisms:
11	(1)~\emph{Registry override}: the semantic constraint forces a domain-compatible type that conflicts with the entity's previously registered type.
12	The entity appears in multiple relations with different type requirements, and the per-relation mask selects the locally valid type without consulting prior assignments.
13	(2)~\emph{Grammar-first fallback} (\S\ref{sec:interaction}): when the semantic mask conflicts with all grammar-valid tokens, the semantic layer is dropped entirely, allowing the grammar layer to generate any structurally valid type---which may differ from the entity's registered type.
14	
15	These mechanisms have sharply different model profiles.
16	Qwen3-8B triggers zero grammar-first fallbacks across all experiments, attributing 100\% of its CF violations to registry override.
17	Llama-3.1-8B, by contrast, triggers 5{,}882 fallbacks on SciERC (10.7 per document) and 57{,}825 on DocRED (63.8 per document), making grammar-first fallback the dominant CF source.
18	This asymmetry is consistent with the cross-model CF gap: Qwen achieves CF\,=\,2.57\% on DocRED vs.\ Llama's 12.02\%, despite both using identical constraint configurations.
19	The difference traces to Llama's less calibrated type predictions, which more frequently conflict with the semantic mask's valid set, triggering fallback.

24	\paragraph{Fallback Behavior and Effective Coverage.}
25	\label{app:fallback-coverage}

27	\emph{Grammar-first fallback} (36.6\% of type-bearing positions on SciERC) occurs when $S(t) \cap G(t) = \emptyset$: the semantic layer deactivates as a safety valve, preserving structural validity at the cost of potential type violations---these events account for the residual DR that persists after constraint enforcement.
28	\emph{Registry-consistent fallback} (4.5\%) occurs when the entity's registered type conflicts with domain/range constraints; the system defaults to the registered type for cross-triple consistency.
29	Together, these mechanisms produce the characteristic profile of composable constraint systems: residual DR traces to grammar-first fallback events, while CF violations arise from registry override events where per-relation enforcement assigns conflicting types.

31	We define \emph{effective semantic constraint coverage} as $1 - f_{\text{gf}}$, where $f_{\text{gf}}$ is the grammar-first fallback rate.
32	On SciERC, this yields 63.4\% coverage---at 63.4\% of type-bearing positions, the semantic layer actively constrains generation.

\section{Extended Discussion}\label{app:discussion}

%%% CF Dual Mechanism %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, llama_scierc_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1

\paragraph{CF Dual Mechanism.}
CF violations arise from two distinct mechanisms:
(1)~\emph{Registry override}: the semantic constraint forces a domain-compatible type that conflicts with the entity's previously registered type.
The entity appears in multiple relations with different type requirements, and the per-relation mask selects the locally valid type without consulting prior assignments.
(2)~\emph{Grammar-first fallback} (\S\ref{sec:interaction}): when the semantic mask conflicts with all grammar-valid tokens, the semantic layer is dropped entirely, allowing the grammar layer to generate any structurally valid type---which may differ from the entity's registered type.

These mechanisms have sharply different model profiles.
Qwen3-8B triggers zero grammar-first fallbacks across all experiments, attributing 100\% of its CF violations to registry override.
Llama-3.1-8B, by contrast, triggers 5{,}882 fallbacks on SciERC (10.7 per document) and 57{,}825 on DocRED (63.8 per document), making grammar-first fallback the dominant CF source.
This asymmetry is consistent with the cross-model CF gap: Qwen achieves CF\,=\,2.57\% on DocRED vs.\ Llama's 12.02\%, despite both using identical constraint configurations.
The difference traces to Llama's less calibrated type predictions, which more frequently conflict with the semantic mask's valid set, triggering fallback.

%%% Fallback Behavior and Effective Coverage %%%
% exp_ids: cf_fallback_ablation_scierc (final data)

\paragraph{Fallback Behavior and Effective Coverage.}
\label{app:fallback-coverage}
The two-layer architecture produces two distinct fallback mechanisms with different semantic consequences.
\emph{Grammar-first fallback} (36.6\% of type-bearing positions on SciERC) occurs when $S(t) \cap G(t) = \emptyset$: the semantic layer deactivates as a safety valve, preserving structural validity at the cost of potential type violations---these events account for the residual DR that persists after constraint enforcement.
\emph{Registry-consistent fallback} (4.5\%) occurs when the entity's registered type conflicts with domain/range constraints; the system defaults to the registered type for cross-triple consistency.
Together, these mechanisms produce the characteristic profile of composable constraint systems: residual DR traces to grammar-first fallback events, while CF violations arise from registry override events where per-relation enforcement assigns conflicting types.

We define \emph{effective semantic constraint coverage} as $1 - f_{\text{gf}}$, where $f_{\text{gf}}$ is the grammar-first fallback rate.
On SciERC, this yields 63.4\% coverage---at 63.4\% of type-bearing positions, the semantic layer actively constrains generation.
This metric directly quantifies the enabling dependency (\S\ref{sec:interaction}): it measures the fraction of decoding steps where both constraint layers are jointly active, providing a fine-grained view beyond aggregate violation rates.
Qwen3-8B, with zero grammar-first fallbacks, achieves 100\% effective coverage on SciERC, consistent with its lower residual DR (0.93\% vs.\ Llama's 0.08\%).

%%% CF-DR Trade-off Analysis %%%
% exp_ids: cf_fallback_ablation_scierc (CF fallback vs full_s1 baseline)

\paragraph{CF-DR Trade-off Analysis.}
\label{app:cf-dr-tradeoff}

CF violations are the most prominent residual limitation of OntoCoDec under zero-shot decoding (9.90\% on SciERC, up to 12.02\% on Llama DocRED).
We treat this honestly: per-relation independent enforcement cannot eliminate CF without trading it against DR.
Table~\ref{tab:cf-dr-tradeoff} reports a pilot ablation in which we replace the grammar-first fallback with a CF-priority fallback that forces the entity's registered type when it conflicts with $\sigma(r)$.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l rrrr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Configuration} & \textbf{DR\,(\%)} & \textbf{CF\,(\%)} & \textbf{DR+CF} & \textbf{$f_{\text{gf}}$\,(\%)} \\
\midrule
Full S1 (baseline) & 0.93 & 9.90 & 10.83 & --- \\
CF fallback        & 14.78 & 0.04 & 14.82 & 36.64 \\
\midrule
$\Delta$ & $+$13.85 & $-$9.86 & $+$3.99 & --- \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{CF-DR trade-off pilot on SciERC (Qwen3-8B, 551 documents; \texttt{w1\_cf\_fallback\_scierc\_pilot}). CF fallback eliminates CF but re-routes violations to DR, increasing total violations (DR+CF) by 3.99\,pp. $f_{\text{gf}}$: grammar-first fallback rate at type-bearing positions.}
\label{tab:cf-dr-tradeoff}
\end{table}

The CF fallback variant nearly eliminates CF (9.90\%\,$\to$\,0.04\%, $-$9.86\,pp) but at the cost of a 15.9$\times$ increase in DR (0.93\%\,$\to$\,14.78\%, $+$13.85\,pp).
% exp_id: w1_cf_fallback_scierc_pilot: DR=0.1478, CF=0.0004, f_gf=0.3664
This is not a net improvement: total violations (DR+CF) rise from 10.83\% to 14.82\% ($+$3.99\,pp), so the change \emph{re-routes} violations rather than reducing them.
The mechanism is mechanical: each token position with conflicting masks must commit to one violation type; when the CF fallback forces the system to emit the entity's registered type even though it lies outside $\sigma(r)$, the resulting triple satisfies cross-entity consistency but violates domain/range.
The grammar-first fallback is triggered at 36.64\% of type-bearing positions, indicating that this conflict is structural, not a tunable hyperparameter.

We interpret this as a fundamental tension in composable constraint systems with \emph{per-relation independent} enforcement: enforcement priority can be allocated between DR and CF but cannot independently minimize both.
Within this design, the current full S1 configuration sits near the Pareto frontier of the trade-off, achieving 0.93\% DR at the cost of 9.90\% CF.
The CF residual is concentrated in schema ambiguity rather than enforcement failure: 63.3\% of CF violations on SciERC involve the catch-all \textsc{Generic} type (Table~\ref{tab:cf-distribution}), which competes with every content type depending on anaphoric vs.\ referential use---a distinction the per-slot decoder cannot resolve without document-level coreference.

Two complementary paths can lower CF without re-routing it to DR.
(i)~\emph{Reduce the baseline conflict rate.} Composing OntoCoDec with LoRA fine-tuning on SciERC reduces CF by 88\% relative to the zero-shot setting (9.90\%\,$\to$\,1.18\%; Table~\ref{tab:composability}), because the fine-tuned model's per-slot type predictions agree more often with the entity registry, so the per-relation mask and the registry intersect more frequently.
% exp_id: w5_lora_scierc_constrained_eval: CF=0.0118
The remaining 1.18\% still traces to \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X schema ambiguity, so this path is empirically validated on one dataset and one fine-tuning method but does not generalize without further evidence.
(ii)~\emph{Replace per-relation enforcement with global entity-level type consensus during decoding.} This is outside the scope of OntoCoDec's forward-only autoregressive design and is left to future work.

%%% Dual-Factor Quantitative Analysis %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_docred_full_s1,
%          llama_scierc_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1

\paragraph{Dual-Factor Quantitative Analysis.}
\label{app:dual-factor}

Figure~\ref{fig:dual-factor-scatter} plots residual DR against the product $\bar{\tau} \times \text{RV}_{\text{baseline}}$ for all four model$\times$dataset configurations.
A linear fit yields $y = 0.366x - 0.138$ with $R^2 = 0.886$ ($n{=}4$; we do not report a $p$-value given the small sample size).
The strong fit is consistent with the dual-factor pattern described in \S\ref{sec:composition}: configurations with higher tightness and higher baseline violation rate exhibit proportionally higher residual DR after constraint enforcement.
The two DocRED points (high $\bar{\tau}{=}0.842$) separate cleanly from the two SciERC points (low $\bar{\tau}{=}0.333$), and within each dataset the model with higher baseline RV shows higher residual DR.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=0.75\columnwidth]{figures/dual_factor_scatter.pdf}
\caption{Residual DR vs.\ $\bar{\tau} \times \text{RV}_{\text{baseline}}$ across four model$\times$dataset configurations.
Linear fit: $y = 0.366x - 0.138$, $R^2 = 0.886$.}
\label{fig:dual-factor-scatter}
\end{figure}

%%% Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact (moved from §7) %%%
% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),
%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)

\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}
The divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\,pp, $p < 0.001$) and SciERC ($+$0.13\,pp, $p = 0.58$) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary relation names.
DocRED's baseline RV of 29.66\% produces 5{,}189 OOV predictions counted as false positives; eliminating them yields a significant precision gain.
SciERC's baseline RV is only 1.39\% (24 OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.
Llama-3.1-8B's lower baseline RV (16.03\%) yields a smaller but directionally consistent improvement ($+$0.29\,pp vs.\ $+$0.50\,pp), confirming that F1 gain magnitude is proportional to baseline OOV rate.
% exp_ids: phase0_docred_unconstrained, phase0_scierc_unconstrained
% exp_ids: llama_docred_unconstrained (RV=16.03%), llama_docred_full_s1 (R-F1 delta=+0.29pp)

%%% Paragraph 1: Low F1 Practical Significance %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (R-F1=8.36%), phase2_docred_full_s1 (R-F1=8.23%),
%          phase0_scierc_unconstrained (DR=15.37%), phase2_docred_unconstrained (DR=18.46%)

\paragraph{Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1.}
Our reported relation F1 of approximately 8\% on both SciERC and DocRED reflects the inherent difficulty of zero-shot closed IE, where the model receives no task-specific training examples.
For reference, supervised state-of-the-art systems on SciERC achieve approximately 49--53\% relation F1 with full training data~\citep{zhong2021frustratingly,ye2022packed}.
Constraint enforcement operates largely independently of the extraction model's intrinsic capability: it restricts the output space to ontologically valid triples regardless of the underlying model's accuracy.
When applied to fine-tuned models that reach competitive F1 levels, the same constraints remain necessary---Phase~0 analysis confirms that even well-prompted models exhibit non-trivial violation rates (15.37\% DR on SciERC, 18.46\% on DocRED).
% exp_ids: phase0_scierc_unconstrained, phase2_docred_unconstrained
In our evaluation, F1 serves as a \emph{control variable} verifying that constraint enforcement does not degrade extraction quality, not as an optimization target.
The contribution of this work is the constraint enforcement method itself; the zero-shot setting isolates its effect from confounds introduced by task-specific fine-tuning.

%%% Paragraph 4: Decoding-Time vs. Post-Hoc Enforcement %%%
% exp_ids: posthoc_filtering_baseline, phase2_scierc_full_s1 (R-F1=8.36%),
%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (R-F1=8.23%, ET=0%)

\paragraph{Decoding-Time vs.\ Post-Hoc Enforcement.}
Post-hoc filtering---generating triples without constraints, then removing schema-violating predictions---yields higher precision and consequently higher F1 than OntoCoDec on both datasets (SciERC 8.63 vs.\ 8.36; DocRED 9.61 vs.\ 8.23).
% posthoc: SciERC F1=8.63, DocRED F1=9.61; OntoCoDec: SciERC R-F1=8.36, DocRED R-F1=8.23
However, this precision gain comes at substantial cost.
On DocRED, post-hoc filtering discards 48.1\% of all predicted triples, including 127 true positives (11.2\% of correct predictions), reducing recall from 9.46\% to 8.40\%.
% posthoc_docred: rejection=48.1%, tp_lost=127/1137, R: 9.46→8.40
Entity type violations remain unresolved (ET\,=\,2.47\% vs.\ OntoCoDec's 0\%), as filtering targets only domain/range and vocabulary violations.
% posthoc_docred: ET_residual=2.47%; phase2_docred_full_s1: ET=0%
OntoCoDec's decoding-time approach avoids this information loss by guiding generation toward compliant outputs rather than discarding non-compliant ones, preserving both recall and entity type validity.
The two strategies are complementary: post-hoc filtering can serve as an additional safety net for residual violations that decoding-time enforcement does not fully resolve.

%%% CF Violation Distribution %%%
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=245), llama_scierc_full_s1 (CF=162),
%          phase2_docred_full_s1 (CF=2670), llama_docred_full_s1 (CF=3824)

\paragraph{Cross-Field Violation Distribution.}
\label{app:cf-distribution}

Table~\ref{tab:cf-distribution} reports the complete distribution of conflicting-type pairs for SciERC full S1 (245 CF violations, all pairwise---no mention triggered $\geq$3 types).
Conflicts involving the \textsc{Generic} type account for 63.3\% (155/245) of all violations.
\textsc{Generic} is SciERC's anaphoric/placeholder label (``this approach'', ``the method''), which competes with every content type depending on whether the mention is used anaphorically or referentially---a distinction the per-slot constrained decoder cannot resolve without document-level coreference.

The pattern generalizes across models and datasets: on Llama-3.1-8B SciERC, \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{OtherScientificTerm} remains the top pair (53/162, 32.7\%); on DocRED, the analogous catch-all type \textsc{MISC} drives 76.6\% of Qwen's CF violations.
Under unconstrained decoding, CF rates collapse to $\leq$1\% on both datasets, confirming that CF violations are a side-effect of per-slot type commitment rather than a model deficiency.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr r@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Conflicting Type Pair} & \textbf{Count} & \textbf{\%} \\
\midrule
Generic $\leftrightarrow$ OtherScientificTerm & 85 & 34.7 \\
Generic $\leftrightarrow$ Material & 35 & 14.3 \\
Generic $\leftrightarrow$ Metric & 30 & 12.2 \\
Method $\leftrightarrow$ Task & 20 & 8.2 \\
Material $\leftrightarrow$ Method & 17 & 6.9 \\
OtherScientificTerm $\leftrightarrow$ Task & 12 & 4.9 \\
\midrule
10 further pairs (each $\leq$3.3\%) & 46 & 18.8 \\
\midrule
\textbf{Total} & \textbf{245} & 100.0 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{CF violation distribution on SciERC full S1 (Qwen3-8B, 551 documents).
All 245 violations are pairwise conflicts.
Conflicts involving \textsc{Generic} account for 63.3\%.}
\label{tab:cf-distribution}
\end{table}

%%% Per-Relation DR Elimination under Fine-Tuning %%%
% exp_ids: lora_scierc_unconstrained, lora_scierc_full_s1

\paragraph{Per-Relation DR Elimination under Fine-Tuning.}
\label{app:lora-per-relation}

Table~\ref{tab:lora-per-relation} presents the per-relation breakdown of DR elimination when OntoCoDec is composed with LoRA fine-tuning on SciERC.
Fine-tuning alone eliminates DR on four of seven relations but leaves non-zero violations on the three tightest-constraint relations: \textsc{Evaluate-for} ($\tau{=}0.361$, 13.13\%), \textsc{Part-of} ($\tau{=}0.417$, 5.77\%), and \textsc{Compare} ($\tau{=}0.528$, 5.00\%).
Adding OntoCoDec constraints eliminates all remaining violations across all relations.
One \textsc{Evaluate-for} triple (99\,$\to$\,98) is redirected to \textsc{Used-for} (634\,$\to$\,635) by token-level masking: the head entity's registered type falls outside \textsc{Evaluate-for}'s domain, and the semantic mask steers generation to the nearest valid relation.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r rr rr@{}}

\paragraph{Fine-Tuned Four-Way Ablation.}
\label{app:ft-ablation}

Table~\ref{tab:ft-ablation} presents the four-way constraint ablation on fine-tuned models across both datasets, isolating each layer's contribution when the base model has already internalized schema knowledge.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3.5pt}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rr@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Model} & \textbf{Mode} & \textbf{DR\,(\%)\,$\downarrow$} & \textbf{R-F1\,$\uparrow$} \\
\midrule
\multirow{8}{*}{SciERC}
  & \multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
    & Unconstrained & 1.95 & 43.86 \\
  & & Grammar       & 1.90 & 43.86 \\
  & & Semantic      & 0.60 & 43.69 \\

  & \multirow{4}{*}{Llama-3.1-8B}
    & Unconstrained & 1.11 & 45.45 \\

\midrule
\multirow{8}{*}{DocRED}
  & \multirow{4}{*}{Qwen3-8B}
    & Unconstrained & 0.76 & 40.86 \\
  & & Grammar       & 0.61 & 40.85 \\
  & & Semantic      & 0.21 & 40.89 \\
  & & Full S1       & \textbf{0.01} & 40.56 \\

  & \multirow{4}{*}{Llama-3.1-8B}

\bottomrule

\caption{Four-way constraint ablation on fine-tuned models (LoRA, 2 models $\times$ 2 datasets).

\label{tab:ft-ablation}
\end{table}

The grammar layer is effectively a no-op for fine-tuned models across all four settings: RV and ET are already 0\% without constraints, and grammar-only DR change is $<$0.2\,pp (4/4 settings).
The semantic layer is the sole effective DR defense under fine-tuning, independently reducing DR by 39--72\% across all settings (SciERC: Qwen $-$69\%, Llama $-$41\%; DocRED: Qwen $-$72\%, Llama $-$39\%).
Adding both layers achieves near-complete elimination (DR\,$\leq$\,0.20\% in all 4 settings), confirming that even after fine-tuning, the semantic layer's pair-based enforcement captures violations that training alone cannot eliminate---specifically on tight-constraint relations where the valid type-pair space is small.

%%% Post-Hoc Filtering Comparison (Extended) %%%
% exp_ids: posthoc_*_zs, posthoc_*_ft

\paragraph{Post-Hoc Filtering: Extended Comparison.}
\label{app:posthoc-extended}

Table~\ref{tab:posthoc-extended} presents the full comparison across all six zero-shot and four fine-tuned configurations.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}

\begin{tabular}{@{}lll rrr l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Setting} & \textbf{Model} & \textbf{Dataset} & \textbf{Reject\%} & \textbf{R-F1$_{\text{ph}}$} & \textbf{R-F1$_{\text{cd}}$} & \textbf{Winner} \\
\midrule
\multirow{6}{*}{ZS}
  & Qwen    & SciERC & 16.8 & 8.63  & 8.36  & ph \\
  & Llama   & SciERC & 13.9 & 2.71  & 2.54  & ph \\
  & Mistral & SciERC & 20.3 & 3.94  & 3.67  & ph \\
  & Qwen    & DocRED & 48.1 & 9.61  & 8.23  & ph \\
  & Llama   & DocRED & 42.2 & 7.44  & 6.27  & ph \\
  & Mistral & DocRED & \textbf{73.7} & 3.85  & \textbf{5.52} & cd \\
\midrule
\multirow{4}{*}{FT}
  & Qwen    & SciERC & 1.95 & 43.94 & 43.77 & ph \\
  & Llama   & SciERC & 1.11 & 45.23 & 45.47 & cd \\
  & Qwen    & DocRED & 1.03 & 41.11 & 40.56 & ph \\
  & Llama   & DocRED & 0.64 & 43.92 & 44.23 & cd \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}%
\caption{Post-hoc filtering (ph) vs.\ constrained decoding (cd).
In zero-shot settings, post-hoc F1 is higher in 5/6 groups (precision-dominated), but constrained decoding preserves higher recall in all 6/6 groups.
At reject rate $>$70\% (Mistral DocRED), post-hoc F1 collapses below constrained.
Under fine-tuning, rejection rates drop to 0.6--2.0\% and the two strategies are equivalent ($\Delta \leq 0.55$\,pp; each wins two groups).
F1 $\times$100.}
\label{tab:posthoc-extended}
\end{table}

The crossover point occurs when post-hoc rejection exceeds $\sim$70\%: Mistral DocRED rejects 73.7\% of predicted triples, discarding enough true positives that constrained decoding's recall advantage dominates ($+$1.67\,pp).
OntoCoDec's advantage thus scales with violation severity---precisely when constraints are most needed, post-hoc filtering is most destructive.
Under fine-tuning, both strategies converge because few violations remain to filter or constrain ($\Delta \leq 0.55$\,pp across all four FT groups, with each strategy winning two).

%%% FT Latency %%%

\paragraph{Fine-Tuned Latency Profiling.}
\label{app:ft-latency}
Under LoRA fine-tuning (Qwen3-8B, SciERC, 100 documents, RTX PRO 6000), per-document inference times are: unconstrained 2.594\,s, grammar-only 2.637\,s ($+$1.7\%), semantic-only 2.625\,s ($+$1.2\%), full S1 2.655\,s ($+$2.3\%, $p{<}0.0001$ paired $t$-test).
The combined overhead is sub-additive (2.3\% $<$ 1.7\%$+$1.2\%) because fine-tuned models produce fewer grammar-first fallback events (the semantic mask conflicts with grammar-valid tokens less often when per-slot predictions are better calibrated), reducing the number of active masking calls per document.
Compared to the zero-shot regime (Table~\ref{tab:runtime}), absolute overhead decreases from seconds-scale to milliseconds-scale: the fine-tuned model generates shorter, more structured outputs, compressing total generation time from 8.69\,s to 2.594\,s per document.

%%% Fuzzy Relation Matching %%%

\paragraph{Relation Matching Protocol.}
\label{app:fuzzy-matching}
Relation F1 evaluation uses fuzzy normalization to handle model-specific formatting variants (e.g., underscores vs.\ spaces, abbreviations).
A predicted relation $r_p$ matches gold relation $r_g$ if: (1)~exact string match after case-insensitive normalization, or (2)~token overlap $>$80\% \emph{and} edit distance $\leq 2$.
This protocol affects primarily Mistral, which produces underscore-separated variants (e.g., ``head\_of\_government'' for ``head of government'').
On Mistral DocRED, fuzzy matching contributes 98 additional TPs ($+$0.84\,pp R-F1; strict R-F1\,=\,3.50\% vs.\ fuzzy 4.34\%).
For Qwen and Llama under grammar constraints, the grammar layer enforces exact relation names, making fuzzy matching irrelevant (0 additional matches).
All F1 figures in the main text use fuzzy normalization consistently across all models and conditions.

(SIGDIAL 2024) "Dialogue Ontology Relation Extraction via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding" 已将 ontology terms 和 relations 作为 constrained decoding 的约束目标用于关系抽取，且通过 constraining decoding to ontology terms 来减少幻觉。虽然 DORE 的技术路径不同（CoT decoding + confidence threshold vs. logit masking），但 "first" claim 需要更精确地限定技术边界（e.g., "first to enforce domain/range *pair-based* constraints via stateful token masking"），并明确区分与 DORE 的差异。

- 建议修改方向：在 §1 或 §3 开头明确一段话阐述：代码生成的 type system → automaton → mask pipeline 为何不能直接用于 IE（entity types 非 declared 而是 extracted、需要 stateful registry、ontology 是 flat 而非 hierarchical），以及 OntoCoDec 的具体技术解决方案。

- 具体位置：§5 全部实验

- 具体位置：§5 全部
- 问题：论文的核心实验设计是：约束违反率下降 = 成功。这是 tautological 的——施加约束当然会减少约束违反。真正需要证明的是：减少违反是否带来下游价值？论文用 F1 作为 "control variable" 证明无害，但 F1-neutral 不等于有用。Appendix B 的 post-hoc filtering 对比显示 post-hoc 在大多数情况下 F1 还更高（5/6 zero-shot 设置）。

- 具体位置：§5.1 (section3_violation_landscape.tex)
- 问题：这一节同时承担三个角色：(1) 实验设置描述、(2) 基线违反率分析（这是 motivation）、(3) schema-informed prompting 对比（这是 baseline experiment）。逻辑上，violation landscape 分析应放在 §2 Background 或 §3 Method 的 motivation 部分，实验设置应独立为一个清晰的 subsection。当前安排使读者在 §5 开头看到 motivation 内容感到困惑。

- 具体位置：全文

- 建议：添加 "Code and data will be released upon acceptance" 或类似声明。

- §3.5 "Decoding Strategies" 中 S2 的描述过于简略（"Detailed comparison is provided in the appendix"），但 S2 在 Table 2 中有数据，建议补充 1-2 句 S2 的实际结果总结。
- §4 equation (2) 定义 tightness 时用 $\tau(r)$ 与 entity type 集合 $\mathcal{T}$ 的符号冲突——$\tau$ 既用于 entity type ($\tau_i$) 又用于 tightness 函数。
- Table 3 footnote "Parse failures: Qwen DocRED 12→11 (S1 1.10%)" 意义不清——12→11 是什么？documents 数？需要更明确的解释。
- Appendix B "Relation Matching Protocol" 使用 fuzzy matching（token overlap >80% + edit distance ≤2）。这个协议对 Mistral 的 F1 贡献 +0.84pp，应在主文 §5.3 简要提及以确保评价一致性透明。
- `\bibliography{relwork_new_entries}` 使用单一 bib 文件命名为 "relwork_new_entries" 不太规范，建议改为 "references.bib" 或 "main.bib"。

---

## Missing References

1. **Vukovic et al. (SIGDIAL 2024)** — "Dialogue Ontology Relation Extraction via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding"。直接使用 constrained decoding 进行 ontology-based relation extraction，与 OntoCoDec 的问题设定高度相关。**必须引用并区分。**

2. **"A Survey of Generative Information Extraction" (COLING 2025)** — 综述性文献，有助于定位本工作在 generative IE 领域的位置。建议引用。

3. **PARSE (Shen et al., EMNLP 2025 Industry)** — "LLM Driven Schema Optimization for Reliable Entity Extraction"，使用 schema guardrails 减少 extraction errors 92%。不同路径但相关。可选引用。

4. **Schema Reinforcement Learning (ACL 2025)** — "Learning to Generate Structured Output with Schema Reinforcement Learning"。Training-time schema compliance 方法，与 OntoCoDec 的 inference-time 方法互补。可选引用。

---

## 主要优势

1. **问题定义清晰且有数据支撑**：violation landscape 分析（Table 1, Figure 1）令人信服地证明了问题的普遍性和严重性，per-relation tightness 分析提供了有解释力的框架。

2. **实验设计全面且诚实**：3 模型 × 2 数据集 × 多消融 × composability with fine-tuning × runtime profiling × post-hoc comparison。CF trade-off 的坦诚讨论（包括 CF-DR trade-off ablation, Table 5）体现了学术诚信。

3. **实用性强**：runtime overhead 仅 2-5%，training-free，与 fine-tuning 正交组合后 DR≤0.20%——这是一个可以直接部署的系统。

4. **形式化分析有价值**：§4 的 decidability taxonomy（local / prefix-decidable / non-local）和 non-rectangularity 分析为 constrained decoding 在 IE 中的应用提供了理论框架。

5. **相关工作覆盖度高**：§6 + Appendix A 覆盖了 5 个 paradigm，引用了 2024-2026 的最新工作（IterGen ICLR 2025, CRANE ICML 2025, BoostCD EMNLP 2025, Zhou 2026 等），分类合理。

---

## Questions for Authors

**Q1**: 为什么不与 GCD (Geng et al., EMNLP 2023) 做直接实验对比？GCD 是你们同一实验室的前作，使用 input-dependent grammars 做 IE，且开源。OntoCoDec 的 grammar layer 与 GCD 的关系是什么——是改进、扩展还是不同的技术路线？

**Q2**: CF 增加是否会传播到下游任务？例如，如果将抽取的 triples 用于 knowledge graph construction，一个实体有两个冲突类型对下游的影响是什么？是否有初步评估？

**Q3**: Abstract 中的 $R^2=0.886$ (n=4) 是否可以扩展到包含 Mistral 的 6 个数据点？如果加入 Mistral (56.94% DR SciERC, 57.42% DR DocRED)，拟合是否依然成立？

**Q4**: 在 fine-tuned 设置下（Table 7），grammar layer 是 no-op。这是否意味着 OntoCoDec 对 fine-tuned 系统的实际价值仅来自 semantic layer？如果是，"two-layer compiled constraint framework" 的 framing 是否过度强调了 grammar layer 的贡献？

**Q5**: 论文的 tokenizer 假设（"each entity type maps to a unique first subword token"）限制了方法的泛化性。对于有 50+ entity types 的大型本体（如 Wikidata 的完整 entity type hierarchy），prefix-tree masking 的工程复杂度和 runtime 开销预期如何？

- 问题：论文正确识别了 PLDI 2025 (Mündler et al.) 为 "closest mechanistic analog"，但主文 §6 仅用两句话打发（"Synchromesh, PICARD, MGD, and PLDI2025 enforce type and scope constraints in code generation; OntoCoDec migrates this paradigm to IE"）。真正的 novelty 需要更清晰地回答：migrating 这个 paradigm 的技术困难在哪里？如果答案是 "entity registry populated during generation"（即 constraint target 需要从 free text 推断而非从 declared type annotation 读取），这个贡献在主文中几乎看不到突出表述，只在 Appendix A 有详细讨论。
- 为什么影响接收：如果核心区分点只出现在 Appendix 而非 §1/§3/§6 主文，reviewer 容易判断为 "incremental migration"。
- 建议修改方向：在 §1 或 §3 开头明确一段话阐述：代码生成的 type system → automaton → mask pipeline 为何不能直接用于 IE（entity types 非 declared 而是 extracted、需要 stateful registry、ontology 是 flat 而非 hierarchical），以及 OntoCoDec 的具体技术解决方案。

**N3** [critical] 缺少与同领域 constrained decoding IE 系统的直接实验对比

- 具体位置：§5 全部实验
- 问题：论文对比的 baseline 是 unconstrained decoding 和 post-hoc filtering。但同领域已有 constrained decoding IE 系统：GCD (Geng et al., EMNLP 2023) 来自同一实验室（EPFL dlab），直接在 IE 任务上做 grammar-constrained decoding；BoostCD (Sakota et al., EMNLP 2025) 同样针对 closed IE 用 constrained decoding + boosting。论文引用了这两篇但未做实验对比。特别是 GCD 使用 input-dependent grammars 做 IE，是 OntoCoDec grammar layer 的直接先驱，不对比就无法证明 semantic layer 的增量价值超过 GCD 已有能力。
- 为什么影响接收：ACL ARR reviewer 会质疑为什么不与最接近的同类方法对比。
- 建议修改方向：至少与 GCD 做定量对比（GCD 公开代码，同一数据集）；如果 GCD 不支持 domain/range 约束（很可能不支持），这本身就是一个有力的区分证据，但需要实验展示而非仅凭论述。

---

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1** [warning] Dual-factor regression ($R^2=0.886$, $n=4$) 不具统计意义

- 具体位置：Abstract line 13, §4 Constraint Tightness paragraph, Appendix B "Dual-Factor Quantitative Analysis"
- 问题：用 4 个数据点拟合线性模型并报告 $R^2=0.886$ 作为 "predictive framework"，这在统计上是不严谨的。4 个点的线性拟合几乎必然得到高 $R^2$（2 自由度，2 参数）。论文自身承认 "we do not report a p-value given the small sample size"，但仍在 Abstract 和 §7 中使用这个数字作为 contribution claim 的一部分。
- 建议：(1) 从 Abstract 中移除 $R^2$ 数字；(2) 将其降级为 "preliminary observation consistent with..."；(3) 如果加入 Mistral 的 4 个数据点（6 model×dataset 配置可用），至少提供 6 点拟合。

**W2** [warning] CF 增加（最高 12.02%）与 "constraint enforcement" 的核心叙事存在张力

- 具体位置：Table 3 (cross-model), §7 Discussion, Limitations
- 问题：OntoCoDec 在减少 DR 的同时引入 CF（SciERC: 0.08%→9.90%; DocRED Llama: 0.17%→12.02%）。论文诚实讨论了这个 trade-off，但叙事上仍以 "constraint enforcement" 定位。一个 "enforcement" 系统引入了新的约束违反类型，需要更直接地在 §1/Abstract 层面承认。Abstract 目前完全不提 CF 增加。
- 建议：在 Abstract 最后加一句 CF caveat（e.g., "with a model-dependent cross-field consistency trade-off mitigated by fine-tuning"），或将标题/定位从 "enforcement" 调整为 "reduction"。

**W3** [warning] 主评价指标是 violation rate reduction 而非下游任务质量——存在循环论证风险

- 具体位置：§5 全部
- 问题：论文的核心实验设计是：约束违反率下降 = 成功。这是 tautological 的——施加约束当然会减少约束违反。真正需要证明的是：减少违反是否带来下游价值？论文用 F1 作为 "control variable" 证明无害，但 F1-neutral 不等于有用。Appendix B 的 post-hoc filtering 对比显示 post-hoc 在大多数情况下 F1 还更高（5/6 zero-shot 设置）。
- 建议：(1) 增加一个下游任务评估（e.g., 用抽取的 triples 做 QA 或 knowledge graph completion，比较有/无 type violation 的影响）；(2) 或者更直接地承认当前贡献是"保证性质"而非"性能提升"，并在 §1 中重新定位。

**W4** [warning] 写作结构问题：§5.1 "Violation Landscape" 混合了 motivation 和 experimental setup

- 具体位置：§5.1 (section3_violation_landscape.tex)
- 问题：这一节同时承担三个角色：(1) 实验设置描述、(2) 基线违反率分析（这是 motivation）、(3) schema-informed prompting 对比（这是 baseline experiment）。逻辑上，violation landscape 分析应放在 §2 Background 或 §3 Method 的 motivation 部分，实验设置应独立为一个清晰的 subsection。当前安排使读者在 §5 开头看到 motivation 内容感到困惑。
- 建议：将 violation landscape 的 motivation 分析（Table 1, Figure 1）提前到 §2.5 或作为独立的 §3.0 "Motivation: Violation Prevalence"。

**W5** [warning] 缺少代码/数据可复现性声明

- 具体位置：全文
- 问题：论文未包含任何关于代码/数据释放的声明。ACL ARR 的 reproducibility 评分维度明确要求作者说明是否会释放代码。Prompt 模板已提供（Appendix），但核心的 semantic layer logits processor 实现、ontology compilation pipeline、entity registry 逻辑均未承诺开源。
- 建议：添加 "Code and data will be released upon acceptance" 或类似声明。

---

## 小问题（不影响接收）

- §3.5 "Decoding Strategies" 中 S2 的描述过于简略（"Detailed comparison is provided in the appendix"），但 S2 在 Table 2 中有数据，建议补充 1-2 句 S2 的实际结果总结。
- §4 equation (2) 定义 tightness 时用 $\tau(r)$ 与 entity type 集合 $\mathcal{T}$ 的符号冲突——$\tau$ 既用于 entity type ($\tau_i$) 又用于 tightness 函数。
- Table 3 footnote "Parse failures: Qwen DocRED 12→11 (S1 1.10%)" 意义不清——12→11 是什么？documents 数？需要更明确的解释。
- Appendix B "Relation Matching Protocol" 使用 fuzzy matching（token overlap >80% + edit distance ≤2）。这个协议对 Mistral 的 F1 贡献 +0.84pp，应在主文 §5.3 简要提及以确保评价一致性透明。
- `\bibliography{relwork_new_entries}` 使用单一 bib 文件命名为 "relwork_new_entries" 不太规范，建议改为 "references.bib" 或 "main.bib"。

---

## Missing References

1. **Vukovic et al. (SIGDIAL 2024)** — "Dialogue Ontology Relation Extraction via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding"。直接使用 constrained decoding 进行 ontology-based relation extraction，与 OntoCoDec 的问题设定高度相关。**必须引用并区分。**

2. **"A Survey of Generative Information Extraction" (COLING 2025)** — 综述性文献，有助于定位本工作在 generative IE 领域的位置。建议引用。

3. **PARSE (Shen et al., EMNLP 2025 Industry)** — "LLM Driven Schema Optimization for Reliable Entity Extraction"，使用 schema guardrails 减少 extraction errors 92%。不同路径但相关。可选引用。

4. **Schema Reinforcement Learning (ACL 2025)** — "Learning to Generate Structured Output with Schema Reinforcement Learning"。Training-time schema compliance 方法，与 OntoCoDec 的 inference-time 方法互补。可选引用。

---

## 主要优势

1. **问题定义清晰且有数据支撑**：violation landscape 分析（Table 1, Figure 1）令人信服地证明了问题的普遍性和严重性，per-relation tightness 分析提供了有解释力的框架。

2. **实验设计全面且诚实**：3 模型 × 2 数据集 × 多消融 × composability with fine-tuning × runtime profiling × post-hoc comparison。CF trade-off 的坦诚讨论（包括 CF-DR trade-off ablation, Table 5）体现了学术诚信。

3. **实用性强**：runtime overhead 仅 2-5%，training-free，与 fine-tuning 正交组合后 DR≤0.20%——这是一个可以直接部署的系统。

4. **形式化分析有价值**：§4 的 decidability taxonomy（local / prefix-decidable / non-local）和 non-rectangularity 分析为 constrained decoding 在 IE 中的应用提供了理论框架。

5. **相关工作覆盖度高**：§6 + Appendix A 覆盖了 5 个 paradigm，引用了 2024-2026 的最新工作（IterGen ICLR 2025, CRANE ICML 2025, BoostCD EMNLP 2025, Zhou 2026 等），分类合理。

---

## Questions for Authors

**Q1**: 为什么不与 GCD (Geng et al., EMNLP 2023) 做直接实验对比？GCD 是你们同一实验室的前作，使用 input-dependent grammars 做 IE，且开源。OntoCoDec 的 grammar layer 与 GCD 的关系是什么——是改进、扩展还是不同的技术路线？

**Q2**: CF 增加是否会传播到下游任务？例如，如果将抽取的 triples 用于 knowledge graph construction，一个实体有两个冲突类型对下游的影响是什么？是否有初步评估？

**Q3**: Abstract 中的 $R^2=0.886$ (n=4) 是否可以扩展到包含 Mistral 的 6 个数据点？如果加入 Mistral (56.94% DR SciERC, 57.42% DR DocRED)，拟合是否依然成立？

**Q4**: 在 fine-tuned 设置下（Table 7），grammar layer 是 no-op。这是否意味着 OntoCoDec 对 fine-tuned 系统的实际价值仅来自 semantic layer？如果是，"two-layer compiled constraint framework" 的 framing 是否过度强调了 grammar layer 的贡献？

**Q5**: 论文的 tokenizer 假设（"each entity type maps to a unique first subword token"）限制了方法的泛化性。对于有 50+ entity types 的大型本体（如 Wikidata 的完整 entity type hierarchy），prefix-tree masking 的工程复杂度和 runtime 开销预期如何？

value.aiTitle: Review schema semantic constrained IE paper

value.content:
[Reviewer 1 审稿意见]:
## Reviewer 1 审稿报告：OntoCoDec

**论文**: OntoCoDec: Type-Constrained Information Extraction via Compiled Ontology Constraints
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 (ARR May 2026 cycle)
**审查侧重**: 方法严谨性 + 实验设计

---

## 总体评分

**Overall**: 3/5 — Findings track acceptance
**一句话总结**: 方法设计干净、消融实验全面、技术上可靠，但 abstract/introduction 对 CF 副作用的系统性省略构成选择性报告问题，R²=0.886 基于 n=4 的"预测框架"声明过度，且对比 post-hoc filtering 的实际优势不具决定性。

---

## 官方维度打分（ACL ARR review form, Feb 2025+）

| 维度 | 分数 | 理由摘要 |
|------|------|----------|
| Soundness | 4/5 | 形式化严谨，消融设计全面，bootstrap 统计测试规范。主要扣分：abstract 选择性报告、n=4 回归过度解读 |
| Excitement | 3/5 | 问题真实且有价值，grammar+semantic 两层架构设计优雅。但实际优势受限于 (a) zero-shot R-F1 仅 ~8%，(b) post-hoc filtering 在多数场景下 F1 更高，(c) CF trade-off 部分抵消核心承诺 |
| Reproducibility | 4/5 | Prompt 模板完整 (Appendix A)，三个公开模型 + 两个公开数据集，解码参数明确 (greedy)，有 bootstrap 参数 (10K)。未提及代码开源计划 |
| Confidence | 4/5 | 逐表核查数值、逐条验证百分比计算、通读全部 appendix |

---

## Must-Fix 问题（影响接收决定）

**N1** [critical] Abstract 和 Introduction 系统性省略 CF 副作用，构成选择性报告

- 具体位置：Abstract (全文)、§1 Introduction (全文)
- 问题：Abstract 声称 "reduces domain/range violations by 94% (15.37%→0.93%) while maintaining extraction F1"，Introduction 列出三条贡献均只提 DR 下降。但 CF (cross-field consistency) 违规从 0.08% 飙升至 9.90%（SciERC, 124× 增幅），Llama DocRED 从 0.17% 升至 12.02%（71× 增幅）。CF 本质上也是本体约束违反——同一实体在不同 triple 中被赋予不同类型。一位只读 abstract 的读者会误以为该方法"几乎消除了本体违规"，而实际上是将一类违规部分转化为另一类。
- 论文正文 §5 和 Appendix B 对 CF 有诚实讨论，但 abstract/intro 的沉默构成科学报告中的 framing bias。
- 为什么影响接收：ARR reviewer guidelines 明确指出 "overclaiming" 和 "presenting speculation as conclusion" 是常见问题。选择性报告核心 trade-off 属于 overclaiming 范畴。
- 建议修改方向：Abstract 中加入一句 CF trade-off 摘要，例如："CF violations increase under zero-shot S1 (up to 12.02%) due to per-relation independent enforcement; fine-tuning reduces this to ≤1.18%." Introduction 的 Contribution 3 也应提及 CF 作为 trade-off 的一部分。

**N2** [critical] R²=0.886 基于 n=4 数据点被过度解读为"预测框架"

- 具体位置：Abstract ("Quantitative analysis reveals that residual DR varies predictably")、§7 Discussion ("the dual-factor pattern (R²=0.886) provides a predictive framework for residual violations")、Appendix B
- 问题：线性回归 y = 0.366x − 0.138 有 2 个自由参数，n=4 仅留 2 个自由度。任意 4 个非共线点的线性拟合都能得到较高 R²。更关键的是，4 个数据点分布为 2 datasets × 2 models，其中两个 dataset 的 tightness 差异巨大（SciERC τ̄=0.333 vs DocRED τ̄=0.842），这意味着 tightness 这一个变量就足以解释大部分方差（本质上是 dataset-level 差异），乘以 baseline RV 的交互项只是在 dataset 内部做 2 点拟合。
- Appendix B 正确地注明 "we do not report a p-value given the small sample size"，但 abstract 和 conclusion 仍将此描述为 "predictive framework"。
- 为什么影响接收：用 n=4 的回归结果在 abstract 中做出定量预测性声明，不符合统计严谨性标准。
- 建议修改方向：将 abstract 中的 "varies predictably" 改为 "is consistent with a dual-factor pattern"；将 conclusion 中的 "predictive framework" 降级为 "descriptive pattern" 或 "consistent with"；在 Appendix 中明确承认 n=4 无法区分是否 tightness 单一因素即可解释。增加 Mistral 的 2 个数据点 (n=6) 或更多 model/dataset 组合以增强说服力。

---

## Should-Fix 问题（影响评分但不一票否决）

**W1** [warning] Parse failure 在约束下增加，构成潜在混淆变量

- 具体位置：Table 4 注释 ("Llama DocRED 68→91")，Limitations §
- 问题：Llama DocRED 下 parse failure 从 68/998 (6.8%) 增至 91/998 (9.1%)，增幅 34%。这些文档被排除在评估之外。如果约束导致更多"困难"文档 parse 失败，则 DR 改善可能部分归因于样本选择偏差（surviving documents 更容易满足约束）。论文在 Qwen DocRED fine-tuned 设置中报告了排除 parse failure 后的数值差异（R-F1 从 -0.30pp 变为 +0.03pp），但 Llama DocRED zero-shot 这一最严重的 parse failure 增长场景缺少类似分析。
- 建议：补充 Llama DocRED zero-shot 的 parse-failure-excluded 分析，或至少讨论为什么约束增加 parse failure（是否因为 grammar-first fallback 累积导致 JSON 结构损坏？）。

**W2** [warning] 与 Post-hoc filtering 对比不充分支持"解码时约束优于后处理"的核心叙事

- 具体位置：Appendix B Table 9、§7 Discussion
- 问题：Post-hoc filtering 在 6 个 zero-shot 配置中 5 个获得更高 R-F1（Table 9）。论文的反驳依据是 (a) OntoCoDec 保持更高 recall、(b) 处理 ET 违规、(c) 在高拒绝率时 post-hoc 崩溃（Mistral DocRED 73.7%）。但对于实践者来说，如果简单的 post-hoc filtering 在大多数场景下 F1 更高，选择 OntoCoDec 的理由需要更强有力的论证。
- 论文将 post-hoc 定位为"互补"策略，但 Introduction 的 framing（"Post-hoc validation wastes compute on discarded outputs and cannot redirect probability mass"）带有否定语气，与实验数据不完全一致。
- 建议：在正文（而非仅 Appendix）中加入 post-hoc 对比的摘要（至少一句话），诚实说明 post-hoc 在多数 zero-shot 场景 F1 更高，OntoCoDec 的优势在 recall 保持和 fine-tuned 场景下的等价性。

**W3** [warning] Zero-shot R-F1 ~8% 的实际意义讨论不足（正文内）

- 具体位置：§5 Experiments（全部 zero-shot 结果）、Appendix B "Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1"
- 问题：SciERC R-F1 = 8.36%，DocRED R-F1 = 8.23%。论文将 F1 定位为"控制变量"——但这一定位仅出现在 Appendix B 的一个段落中，正文和 Introduction 的贡献声明并未明确限定。同时，论文在 DocRED 上高亮 R-F1 gains (+0.50pp, p<0.001) 作为积极结果，存在逻辑不一致：如果 F1 只是控制变量，就不应在正文中强调其改善；如果 F1 重要，那 ~8% 的绝对值需要在正文中正面讨论实际意义。
- 建议：在 §5 实验设置段落中加入 1-2 句正文讨论 zero-shot F1 水平的含义和上下文（如 supervised SOTA ~49-53%），不要仅放在 Appendix。

**W4** [warning] SciERC 5-way 消融 vs DocRED 4-way 消融的不对称性未解释

- 具体位置：Table 2 (SciERC, 5 modes) vs Table 3 (DocRED, 4 modes)
- 问题：SciERC 包含 S2 配置，DocRED 不包含。如果 S2 在 DocRED 上由于 96 relations 的复杂性而不可行或效果差，应明确说明；如果只是篇幅原因，也应说明。
- 建议：加一句解释为什么 DocRED 不测 S2。

**W5** [warning] Semantic-only 模式在 DocRED 上反直觉地增加 ET 违规

- 具体位置：Table 3，Semantic 行 ET = 4.22% vs Unconstrained ET = 2.48%
- 问题：Semantic layer 声称仅在 HeadType/TailType 位置激活（§3.3.2），不应影响 EntityType 位置。但 ET 从 2.48% 几乎翻倍至 4.22%。这可能是 autoregressive 分布扰动的间接效应，但论文未讨论。
- 建议：加一句解释此现象（是否因为 semantic masking 改变了整体 token 分布？）。

**W6** [warning] First-subword-token 唯一性假设限制泛化性

- 具体位置：§3.3 Implementation ("Each τ ∈ E is mapped to the token ID of its first subword token; we pre-verify uniqueness")、Limitations §
- 问题：Limitations 正确指出"ontologies with many types or multi-token type names would require prefix-tree masking, which we have not implemented"。但 §3 的 Method 部分将此作为一个简单的 implementation detail 一笔带过，而这实际上是方法适用范围的根本性限制。如果 entity types 的 first subword token 不唯一（在大型本体中很常见），整个 semantic layer 的 masking 机制就不成立。
- 建议：在 §3 Method 中明确将此列为设计假设（而非 implementation detail），并讨论何时假设成立（小型本体）和不成立（大型本体）。

---

## 小问题（不影响接收）

- **符号冲突**: τ 同时用于 constraint tightness (§4 Eq.3) 和 entity type (§3 Eq.1 中的 τ_i)。建议 tightness 改用 κ 或 ψ。
- **Table 2 S2 行**: CF = 8.03%, R-F1 = 8.03 是数值巧合，但视觉上容易让读者误以为是复制粘贴错误。

**Q1**: CF-DR trade-off 中，Table 6 显示 CF fallback 变体的 total violations (DR+CF) 为 14.82%，比 baseline Full S1 的 10.83% 高 3.99pp。但如果考虑 CF 和 DR 的下游影响不同（例如 CF 可能导致 knowledge graph 中的 entity type 不一致，而 DR 是 triple 级别的错误），是否应对两者赋予不同权重来评估 trade-off？论文目前将 DR 和 CF 简单相加，这是否合理？

- **EnriCo** (Zaratiana et al., 2024): 同上，仅在 Appendix 中引用。EnriCo 使用 ASP 约束在解码时强制类型兼容性，与 OntoCoDec 高度相关。

1. **形式化质量高**：§2-4 的本体定义、constraint tightness、decidability taxonomy、pair-based vs independent enforcement 的论证清晰严谨，数学无歧义。Sequential masking 的必要性论证（non-rectangularity，SciERC 0/7、DocRED 23/96 rectangular）有数据支撑。

2. **消融设计全面且控制变量到位**：5-way/4-way ablation 有效隔离了 grammar layer、semantic layer、S1/S2 的独立贡献。Cross-model 3 模型验证、composability matrix (2 models × 2 datasets × 2 settings)、FT 4-way ablation 覆盖面广。

3. **对 CF trade-off 的正文讨论是诚实的**：§5 明确报告 CF 增加，Appendix B 的 CF-DR 消融（Table 6）用实验证明了 DR 和 CF 的不可独立最小化，CF 分布分析（Table 7）追踪到 Generic 类型的 schema-level 歧义。

4. **Runtime overhead 分析量化了实用性**：Table 5 显示 Full S1 overhead 仅 +2.3%（SciERC）到 +5.4%（DocRED），sub-additive 性质有理论和实验支持。

5. **Post-hoc filtering 对比**（Table 9）虽然结果不完全有利于 OntoCoDec，但论文选择诚实地呈现完整 10 组对比而非挑选有利数据，体现了实验诚信。

[Reviewer 2 审稿意见]:

# Reviewer 2 对 Reviewer 1 审稿意见的逐条回应

---

## Must-Fix 问题

### R1-N1: Abstract/Introduction 省略 CF 副作用

**[AGREE]** — 但对 severity 有不同判断。

我在自己的审稿中将此列为 W2 (Should-Fix)。Reviewer 1 将其列为 Must-Fix。

事实层面完全同意：CF 从 0.08%→9.90%（SciERC, 124×）和 0.17%→12.02%（Llama DocRED, 71×）是重大副作用，Abstract 完全未提及确实构成 framing bias。

但我倾向于 Should-Fix 而非 Must-Fix，理由：
1. §5.2 paragraph 1 最后一句明确报告了 CF 增加（"full constraint enforcement elevates cross-field consistency violations from 0.08% to 9.90%"）
2. §7 Discussion 第二段专门讨论 CF dual mechanism
3. Limitations section 开头就提 CF
4. Appendix B 有完整的 CF-DR trade-off ablation (Table 5)

论文并非隐藏问题，而是在 Abstract/Intro 的 framing 上有偏。这是 "presentation issue" 而非 "integrity issue"。但我同意必须修复——在 Abstract 末尾加一句 CF caveat 即可。

**修改建议一致**：同意 Reviewer 1 的建议，Abstract 加 CF trade-off 摘要。

---

### R1-N2: $R^2=0.886$ (n=4) 过度解读

**[AGREE]** — 完全同意，与我的 W1 重合。

4 个数据点、2 个参数、2 个自由度——$R^2$ 在这种情况下几乎无信息量。即使随机 4 点也经常获得 $R^2>0.8$。

我还注意到一个 Reviewer 1 未提的补充论点：两个 SciERC 点的 tightness ($\bar{\tau}=0.333$) 和两个 DocRED 点的 tightness ($\bar{\tau}=0.842$) 差异巨大，本质上这是一个 "两组各两点" 的比较，tightness 单一变量就能解释大部分方差。$R^2$ 的高值可能仅反映了两个 dataset 的系统性差异，而非 dual-factor 的 predictive power。

建议一致：从 Abstract 移除 $R^2$ 数字，降级为 "descriptive pattern"。增加 Mistral 的 4 个数据点（SciERC + DocRED, unconstrained + S1）可以提供 6-8 点拟合。

---

## Should-Fix 问题

### R1-W1: Parse failure 增加构成混淆变量

**[AGREE]** — 有效问题，我未独立发现。

Table 3 footnote 确认 Llama DocRED parse failure 从 68 增至 91 (6.8%→9.1%)。被排除的文档可能系统性偏向某些关系类型（如长文档或多关系文档），导致 violation rate 和 F1 的计算在非随机子集上进行。

进一步证据：§5.2 composability 部分的脚注提到 "excluding parse-failure documents (+1.4pp increase, 7.1%→8.5%) yields +0.03pp"——这表明 parse failure 确实影响 R-F1 的解读（all-set 报告 -0.30pp，但排除 parse failure 后变为 +0.03pp）。这个信息仅在脚注中，说明作者意识到问题但未充分讨论。

建议：在正文中增加一个 parse failure sensitivity analysis 段落。

---

### R1-W2: Post-hoc filtering 对比不充分支持核心叙事

**[AGREE]** — 与我的 W3 高度重合。

数据事实：Appendix B Table 8 显示 post-hoc filtering 在 5/6 zero-shot 设置上 F1 更高。Introduction 中 "Post-hoc validation wastes compute on discarded outputs and cannot redirect probability mass during decoding" 的表述暗示 post-hoc 是劣势方法，但实验数据不支持这一判断（至少在 F1 指标上）。

但我要补充一点 Reviewer 1 未提到的平衡观点：
- OntoCoDec 在 6/6 zero-shot 设置中 recall 更高（Table 8 隐含）
- 当 rejection rate > 70% (Mistral DocRED) 时 post-hoc 崩溃，OntoCoDec 胜出
- Fine-tuning 下两者收敛

所以 Introduction 的 framing 不完全错误，但需要 nuance。建议将 "wastes compute" 改为条件性表述（e.g., "becomes increasingly destructive as violation rates rise"），并在 §5 加入 post-hoc 对比的正文摘要。

---

### R1-W3: Zero-shot R-F1 ~8% 实际意义讨论不足

**[AGREE]** — 有效但可争辩。

论文在 Appendix B "Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1" 段落中有详细讨论，包括与 supervised SOTA (49-53%) 的对比，以及 "F1 serves as a control variable" 的定位。问题是这段关键论述只在 Appendix 中。

但我对 Reviewer 1 的批评 "正文高亮 DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001 作为积极结果" 有更强的共鸣——如果 F1 只是控制变量，为什么要用 p-value 强调它？这确实存在逻辑不一致。要么 F1 重要（那就讨论 8% 的含义），要么 F1 只是控制（那就不要用统计显著性来高亮它）。

建议：在 §5.2 core result 后加 1-2 句承认 zero-shot F1 的绝对水平较低，引用 Appendix B 的完整讨论。

---

### R1-W4: SciERC 5-way vs DocRED 4-way 消融不对称

**[AGREE]** — 但为 minor issue。

推测原因：DocRED 的 S2 需要两次全文档推理（每文档 ~21s），998 文档的计算成本约 12 GPU-hours，可能是纯工程/资源限制。但论文应说明。一句话足够（e.g., "S2 is omitted on DocRED due to computational cost of two-pass document-level decoding"）。

---

### R1-W5: Semantic-only 模式在 DocRED 上 ET 增加 (2.48%→4.22%)

**[AGREE]** — 好发现，我未独立注意到。

这确实反直觉：semantic layer 声称仅在 HeadType/TailType 位置激活（§3.4.2），不应影响 entity type generation。

推测解释：semantic-only 模式下，没有 grammar layer 保证 entity type token 属于 $\mathcal{E}$。Semantic layer 的 logit masking 可能在某些 prefix 状态下产生 unintended 交互——例如 position detection 误判某个 free-text 位置为 type position，导致 mask 干扰 entity type generation。Table 3 显示 semantic-only 也增加了 RV (29.66%→29.87%)，进一步暗示 semantic layer 在无 grammar 保护下有 side effects。

作者应解释此现象的机制。这也进一步支持了 "enabling dependency" 的论点——semantic layer 不应单独使用。

---

### R1-W6: First-subword-token 唯一性限制泛化性

**[AGREE]** — 与我的 Q5 重合。

§3.4.3 "Implementation" 段将此描述为已验证的 property（"verified for both tokenizers on our two ontologies, 6 entity types each"），但 Limitations 承认 "ontologies with many types or multi-token type names would require prefix-tree masking, which we have not implemented"。

6 个 entity types 的唯一性验证几乎是 trivial 的。真实世界 IE 本体如 Wikidata (7000+ entity types)、UMLS (100+ semantic types)、ACE 2005 (18 entity types) 都远超此规模。这个限制确实是方法论层面的，不仅是工程细节。

建议一致：在 §3.4.3 中将此从 implementation detail 提升为 explicit limitation，说明何时需要 prefix-tree 扩展，并在 Limitations section 中讨论 scalability。

---

## Missing References 评论

**GenIE 和 EnriCo 在正文 §6 中未引用**：[AGREE]。我验证了 section6_related_work.tex——两者仅出现在 appendix_related_work.tex 中。作为与 OntoCoDec 最直接相关的 constrained decoding IE 系统（GenIE: trie-based state constraints; EnriCo: ASP-based type constraints），它们必须出现在主文 §6 而非仅在 Appendix A。

**Zhou et al. (2026) "structure snowballing"**：已在 Appendix A "Quality Impact" 段引用 (`\cite{zhou2026snowballing}`)，但未出现在主文 §6。鉴于 §6 的 "Quality Impact" 段落长度有限，可以接受仅在 Appendix 讨论。INFO 级别，非必须。

---

## 数值一致性核查补充

同意 Reviewer 1 的 ⚠ 标注："DR ↓42--90% on DocRED" 的 42% 来自 Mistral，90% 来自 Llama。Introduction Contribution 3 写 "DR↓42--90% on DocRED" 而 Abstract 也使用此范围。建议在 Introduction 中明确 "(across three model families)"，目前已有但容易被忽略。

---

# Reviewer 2 对 Reviewer 1 审稿意见的逐条回应

---

## Must-Fix 问题

### R1-N1: Abstract/Introduction 省略 CF 副作用

**[AGREE]** — 但对 severity 有不同判断。

我在自己的审稿中将此列为 W2 (Should-Fix)。Reviewer 1 将其列为 Must-Fix。

事实层面完全同意：CF 从 0.08%→9.90%（SciERC, 124×）和 0.17%→12.02%（Llama DocRED, 71×）是重大副作用，Abstract 完全未提及确实构成 framing bias。

但我倾向于 Should-Fix 而非 Must-Fix，理由：
1. §5.2 paragraph 1 最后一句明确报告了 CF 增加（"full constraint enforcement elevates cross-field consistency violations from 0.08% to 9.90%"）
2. §7 Discussion 第二段专门讨论 CF dual mechanism
3. Limitations section 开头就提 CF
4. Appendix B 有完整的 CF-DR trade-off ablation (Table 5)

论文并非隐藏问题，而是在 Abstract/Intro 的 framing 上有偏。这是 "presentation issue" 而非 "integrity issue"。但我同意必须修复——在 Abstract 末尾加一句 CF caveat 即可。

**修改建议一致**：同意 Reviewer 1 的建议，Abstract 加 CF trade-off 摘要。

---

### R1-N2: $R^2=0.886$ (n=4) 过度解读

**[AGREE]** — 完全同意，与我的 W1 重合。

4 个数据点、2 个参数、2 个自由度——$R^2$ 在这种情况下几乎无信息量。即使随机 4 点也经常获得 $R^2>0.8$。

我还注意到一个 Reviewer 1 未提的补充论点：两个 SciERC 点的 tightness ($\bar{\tau}=0.333$) 和两个 DocRED 点的 tightness ($\bar{\tau}=0.842$) 差异巨大，本质上这是一个 "两组各两点" 的比较，tightness 单一变量就能解释大部分方差。$R^2$ 的高值可能仅反映了两个 dataset 的系统性差异，而非 dual-factor 的 predictive power。

建议一致：从 Abstract 移除 $R^2$ 数字，降级为 "descriptive pattern"。增加 Mistral 的 4 个数据点（SciERC + DocRED, unconstrained + S1）可以提供 6-8 点拟合。

---

## Should-Fix 问题

### R1-W1: Parse failure 增加构成混淆变量

**[AGREE]** — 有效问题，我未独立发现。

Table 3 footnote 确认 Llama DocRED parse failure 从 68 增至 91 (6.8%→9.1%)。被排除的文档可能系统性偏向某些关系类型（如长文档或多关系文档），导致 violation rate 和 F1 的计算在非随机子集上进行。

进一步证据：§5.2 composability 部分的脚注提到 "excluding parse-failure documents (+1.4pp increase, 7.1%→8.5%) yields +0.03pp"——这表明 parse failure 确实影响 R-F1 的解读（all-set 报告 -0.30pp，但排除 parse failure 后变为 +0.03pp）。这个信息仅在脚注中，说明作者意识到问题但未充分讨论。

建议：在正文中增加一个 parse failure sensitivity analysis 段落。

---

### R1-W2: Post-hoc filtering 对比不充分支持核心叙事

**[AGREE]** — 与我的 W3 高度重合。

数据事实：Appendix B Table 8 显示 post-hoc filtering 在 5/6 zero-shot 设置上 F1 更高。Introduction 中 "Post-hoc validation wastes compute on discarded outputs and cannot redirect probability mass during decoding" 的表述暗示 post-hoc 是劣势方法，但实验数据不支持这一判断（至少在 F1 指标上）。

但我要补充一点 Reviewer 1 未提到的平衡观点：
- OntoCoDec 在 6/6 zero-shot 设置中 recall 更高（Table 8 隐含）
- 当 rejection rate > 70% (Mistral DocRED) 时 post-hoc 崩溃，OntoCoDec 胜出
- Fine-tuning 下两者收敛

所以 Introduction 的 framing 不完全错误，但需要 nuance。建议将 "wastes compute" 改为条件性表述（e.g., "becomes increasingly destructive as violation rates rise"），并在 §5 加入 post-hoc 对比的正文摘要。

---

### R1-W3: Zero-shot R-F1 ~8% 实际意义讨论不足

**[AGREE]** — 有效但可争辩。

论文在 Appendix B "Practical Significance of Zero-Shot F1" 段落中有详细讨论，包括与 supervised SOTA (49-53%) 的对比，以及 "F1 serves as a control variable" 的定位。问题是这段关键论述只在 Appendix 中。

但我对 Reviewer 1 的批评 "正文高亮 DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001 作为积极结果" 有更强的共鸣——如果 F1 只是控制变量，为什么要用 p-value 强调它？这确实存在逻辑不一致。要么 F1 重要（那就讨论 8% 的含义），要么 F1 只是控制（那就不要用统计显著性来高亮它）。

建议：在 §5.2 core result 后加 1-2 句承认 zero-shot F1 的绝对水平较低，引用 Appendix B 的完整讨论。

---

### R1-W4: SciERC 5-way vs DocRED 4-way 消融不对称

**[AGREE]** — 但为 minor issue。

推测原因：DocRED 的 S2 需要两次全文档推理（每文档 ~21s），998 文档的计算成本约 12 GPU-hours，可能是纯工程/资源限制。但论文应说明。一句话足够（e.g., "S2 is omitted on DocRED due to computational cost of two-pass document-level decoding"）。

---

### R1-W5: Semantic-only 模式在 DocRED 上 ET 增加 (2.48%→4.22%)

**[AGREE]** — 好发现，我未独立注意到。

这确实反直觉：semantic layer 声称仅在 HeadType/TailType 位置激活（§3.4.2），不应影响 entity type generation。

推测解释：semantic-only 模式下，没有 grammar layer 保证 entity type token 属于 $\mathcal{E}$。Semantic layer 的 logit masking 可能在某些 prefix 状态下产生 unintended 交互——例如 position detection 误判某个 free-text 位置为 type position，导致 mask 干扰 entity type generation。Table 3 显示 semantic-only 也增加了 RV (29.66%→29.87%)，进一步暗示 semantic layer 在无 grammar 保护下有 side effects。

作者应解释此现象的机制。这也进一步支持了 "enabling dependency" 的论点——semantic layer 不应单独使用。

---

### R1-W6: First-subword-token 唯一性限制泛化性

**[AGREE]** — 与我的 Q5 重合。

§3.4.3 "Implementation" 段将此描述为已验证的 property（"verified for both tokenizers on our two ontologies, 6 entity types each"），但 Limitations 承认 "ontologies with many types or multi-token type names would require prefix-tree masking, which we have not implemented"。

6 个 entity types 的唯一性验证几乎是 trivial 的。真实世界 IE 本体如 Wikidata (7000+ entity types)、UMLS (100+ semantic types)、ACE 2005 (18 entity types) 都远超此规模。这个限制确实是方法论层面的，不仅是工程细节。

建议一致：在 §3.4.3 中将此从 implementation detail 提升为 explicit limitation，说明何时需要 prefix-tree 扩展，并在 Limitations section 中讨论 scalability。

---

## Missing References 评论

**GenIE 和 EnriCo 在正文 §6 中未引用**：[AGREE]。我验证了 section6_related_work.tex——两者仅出现在 appendix_related_work.tex 中。作为与 OntoCoDec 最直接相关的 constrained decoding IE 系统（GenIE: trie-based state constraints; EnriCo: ASP-based type constraints），它们必须出现在主文 §6 而非仅在 Appendix A。

**Zhou et al. (2026) "structure snowballing"**：已在 Appendix A "Quality Impact" 段引用 (`\cite{zhou2026snowballing}`)，但未出现在主文 §6。鉴于 §6 的 "Quality Impact" 段落长度有限，可以接受仅在 Appendix 讨论。INFO 级别，非必须。

---

同意 Reviewer 1 的 ⚠ 标注："DR ↓42--90% on DocRED" 的 42% 来自 Mistral，90% 来自 Llama。Introduction Contribution 3 写 "DR↓42--90% on DocRED" 而 Abstract 也使用此范围。建议在 Introduction 中明确 "(across three model families)"，目前已有但容易被忽略。

## Reviewer 1 对 Reviewer 2 审稿意见的逐条回应

---

### Must-Fix 问题

**[REBUT] R2-N1: Novelty claim 过度——与 DORE (SIGDIAL 2024) 的区分**

R2 认为 DORE (Vukovic et al., SIGDIAL 2024) 已将 ontology constraints 用于 constrained decoding RE，因此 "first" claim 过度。经查证 DORE 原文，其技术路径是 **Chain-of-Thought decoding + confidence threshold**——在解码空间中生成多个分支，基于置信度阈值选择关系，将输出限制在 ontology terms 范围内。这属于 **output selection level** 的约束，而非 **token-level logit masking**。

OntoCoDec 的 claim 是 "the first to automatically compile IE ontology domain/range constraints into token-level semantic masks"，关键技术边界在 "compile"、"domain/range"、"token-level masks" 三个限定词。DORE 不编译 domain/range 规则到 token-level masks，不维护 entity registry，不做 pair-based sequential type enforcement。两者技术路径根本不同。

**但我同意 DORE 应被引用**作为相关工作（ontology-guided constrained decoding for RE），且 "first" claim 可以更精确——R2 建议的 "first to enforce pair-based domain/range type constraints via compiled stateful logit masks during autoregressive IE" 措辞更准确。

**严重性判断**：降级为 should-fix (warning)，而非 critical。引用缺失应修复，但不构成 novelty 的根本性挑战。

---

**[AGREE with nuance] R2-N2: 与代码生成先驱工作的技术差异阐述不足**

R2 指出 §6 Related Work 仅两句话处理代码生成先驱（"Synchromesh, PICARD, MGD, and [PLDI2025] enforce type and scope constraints in code generation; OntoCoDec migrates this paradigm to IE"），而真正的技术差异（entity registry 在生成中动态构建、constraint target 从 free text 推断而非 declared type annotation）仅在 Appendix A 展开。

这一指摘是成立的。Appendix A 的 "Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code" 段落详细讨论了 PICARD 操作在 "fixed, fully enumerated schema" vs OntoCoDec 的 entity registry 在 "generation 过程中填充"这一根本区别，以及 PLDI2025 作为 "closest mechanistic analog" 的精确技术差异（deep subtyping vs flat domain/range sets，declared types vs free-text inference）。这些论述对建立 novelty 至关重要，但被放在了 Appendix 中，正文读者看不到。

建议在 §3 Method 开头或 §1 Introduction 中用 2-3 句话明确阐述代码生成 type system → automaton → mask pipeline 的已有范式，以及 IE 场景的两个根本区别。

**严重性判断**：同意 should-fix (warning) 级别，但不认为是 critical——novelty 论证存在且正确，只是位置不对（appendix vs main text），属于呈现问题而非实质性缺陷。

---

**[REBUT] R2-N3: 缺少与 GCD/BoostCD 的直接实验对比**

R2 要求与 GCD (Geng et al., EMNLP 2023) 和 BoostCD (Sakota et al., EMNLP 2025) 做直接实验对比。经分析，这一要求存在方法论问题：

**GCD 对比**：GCD 的核心技术是 input-dependent grammar-constrained decoding——即语法层面的约束（vocabulary membership、结构有效性），不具备 cross-field semantic constraint 能力（论文 §6: "limited to syntactic constraints"）。OntoCoDec 的 **Grammar-only 消融行**（Table 2/3）本质上就是 GCD-class approach 的效果上界：
- SciERC Grammar-only: DR 14.84%（几乎不变），RV/ET → 0%
- DocRED Grammar-only: DR 26.17%（反而上升），RV → 0.03%

这就是 grammar-level constrained decoding（GCD 的能力范围）对 DR 的效果。OntoCoDec 的贡献恰恰在于 grammar 之上的 semantic layer——GCD 架构上无法覆盖的部分。要求与 GCD 做 DR reduction 对比，等同于要求论文证明 "semantic constraints 比 syntactic-only constraints 更能减少 semantic violations"，这是 trivially true 且已由消融实验覆盖。

**BoostCD 对比**：BoostCD 是 training-time 策略（combining constrained/unconstrained outputs via boosting），与 OntoCoDec 的 decoding-time approach 在方法论层面正交。论文 §6 已正确定位："complementing our decoding-time approach with a training-time strategy"。

**让步**：论文可以在 §6 或 §5 中加一段明确说明 "Grammar-only row in Table 2/3 represents the capability ceiling of GCD-class approaches, which by design cannot enforce domain/range constraints"，使隐含的对比关系显式化。但要求从零实现 GCD 系统并做全面对比，对于一篇已有 3 models × 2 datasets × 5-way ablation 的论文来说不合理。

**严重性判断**：降级为 info（editorial suggestion），不构成 must-fix。ARR guidelines 明确指出 "Requests for additional experiments qualify as suggestions unless they're essential to the core claims"。核心 claim 是 semantic layer 的价值，已由 grammar-only vs full S1 消融证明。

---

### Should-Fix 问题

**[AGREE] R2-W1: Dual-factor regression 不具统计意义**

与我自己的 N2 [critical] 完全一致。n=4, 2 自由度，R²=0.886 不足以支撑 "predictive framework" 声明。Abstract 中应移除或降级。R2 建议加入 Mistral 数据点（n=6）是可行的改进方向。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W2: CF 增加与 abstract 的张力**

与我自己的 N1 [critical] 完全一致。Abstract 选择性报告 DR reduction 而省略 CF increase（0.08%→9.90% SciERC, 0.17%→12.02% Llama DocRED）构成 framing bias。

---

**[REBUT with partial agreement] R2-W3: "施加约束减少约束违反" 是 tautological 的**

R2 的论点是：constrained decoding reduces constraint violations 是循环论证，需要证明下游价值。

这一表述过度简化了论文的贡献：

1. **非平凡的技术问题**：将 IE ontology 的 domain/range constraints 编译为 autoregressive token-level masks 不是 trivial 的。论文的 novelty 不在于"约束减少违反"这一结论，而在于 HOW——entity registry、sequential masking、grammar-semantic enabling dependency、grammar-first fallback——这些是工程和形式化层面的贡献。

2. **F1 中性是非显然的**：文献中有大量证据表明 constrained decoding 会损害 LLM 生成质量（CRANE, Schall et al., §6 Quality Impact）。论文证明了在 IE 场景下约束不降低 F1（SciERC p=0.58）甚至提升 F1（DocRED p<0.001），这不是 tautological 的。

3. **trade-off 分析是实质性贡献**：CF↔DR trade-off (Table 6, Appendix B)、tightness-driven enforcement ceiling、enabling dependency 的量化——这些经验性发现超越了 "约束减少违反"。

**但 R2 有一个合理的点**：论文可以更明确地将贡献定位为 (a) enforcement mechanism + (b) F1-neutrality guarantee + (c) trade-off characterization，而非仅仅是 violation rate reduction numbers。当前 abstract 的 "reduces DR by 94%" 确实把 violation reduction 当作主要卖点，而这一点确实有循环论证的影子。

**建议**：在 Introduction 中加入一句明确的贡献定位："Our contribution is not that constrained decoding reduces violations—this is expected—but that ontological constraints can be compiled into token-level enforcement with zero F1 cost, composability with fine-tuning, and a characterizable trade-off space."

---

**[AGREE weakly] R2-W4: Violation Landscape 的位置**

R2 建议将 §5.1 "Violation Landscape" 提前到 §2 作为 motivation。这是合理的 editorial suggestion。当前 §5.1 在 "Experiments" section 下但实际功能是 motivation/problem characterization。移到 §2 可改善逻辑流。

但这是 presentation 层面的问题，不影响技术评判。severity 应为 info 而非 warning。

---

**[AGREE] R2-W5: 缺少代码/数据可复现性声明**

与我自己的 Reproducibility 评分 (4/5) 一致。论文提供了 prompt templates、模型名称、数据集名称，但未提及代码开源计划。ARR 鼓励可复现性声明。

---

### R2 Questions 的简要回应

**Q1 (为什么不与 GCD 做实验对比)**: 见上 N3 回应。Grammar-only ablation 行即为 GCD-class baseline。

**Q2 (CF 传播到下游任务)**: 合理担忧。论文 Limitations 提到 "CF type inconsistencies may propagate to downstream tasks (e.g., knowledge graph construction, question answering); the impact of such propagation has not been evaluated"。这是已声明的局限性，但确实需要在正文中更明确讨论。我在自己的 Q1 中也提出了 CF 和 DR 的下游影响权重差异问题。

**Q3 (R² 扩展到 n=6)**: Mistral 有 SciERC 和 DocRED 两个数据点。将其加入后 n=6 仍然很小，但至少 cross-validation 更有说服力。如果 Mistral 数据点偏离 linear fit（考虑到 Mistral 极高的 baseline DR 56-57%），可能反而削弱 R²。作者应尝试并诚实报告。

**Q4 (FT 下 grammar layer 是 no-op，两层 framing 是否过度)**: 合理观察。但论文的定位包含 zero-shot 场景，grammar layer 在 zero-shot 下有明确贡献（RV/ET → 0%，enabling semantic layer）。对于 FT 场景，论文正确报告了 "grammar is a no-op post-fine-tuning" (Table 8 caption)。framing 可以更细致地区分 zero-shot vs FT 的使用建议。

**Q5 (50+ entity types 的 prefix-tree masking 工程复杂度)**: 论文 Limitations 承认 first-subword-token 假设对大型本体不成立，需要 prefix-tree masking。这确实是方法适用范围的限制，我在 W6 中也指出应在 §3 Method 中将此列为设计假设而非 implementation detail。

---

### 与我（R1）审稿的重叠与分歧总结

| R2 Issue | R1 Overlap | 判断 |
|----------|-----------|------|
| R2-N1 DORE | R1 未提及 | REBUT severity (critical→warning)，AGREE cite |
| R2-N2 Code gen novelty | R1 未提及 | AGREE with nuance (presentation issue, not novelty issue) |
| R2-N3 GCD comparison | R1 未提及 | REBUT (ablation already covers) |
| R2-W1 R² on n=4 | R1-N2 [critical] | AGREE |
| R2-W2 CF in abstract | R1-N1 [critical] | AGREE |
| R2-W3 Tautological | R1 未提及 | REBUT with partial agreement |
| R2-W4 §5.1 placement | R1 未提及 | AGREE weakly (info, not warning) |
| R2-W5 Code release | R1 Reproducibility 4/5 | AGREE |

**两位 Reviewer 共同认定的 critical issues**: (1) Abstract 选择性省略 CF，(2) R² overclaim on n=4。这两点应作为 revision 的最高优先级。

**R1 独有的关注点**：parse failure 增加 (W1)、post-hoc filtering 对比叙事 (W2)、semantic-only 反直觉 ET 增加 (W5)、first-subword-token 假设 (W6)。

**R2 独有的关注点**：DORE 引用 (N1)、代码生成差异阐述位置 (N2)、GCD 实验对比 (N3)、tautological 论证风险 (W3)。
